findings.text: MUST-FIX (test fidelity, not production behaviour): test_archive_census_wins_when_it_disagrees_with_the_closure pins the precedence on a state the reconstruction writer cannot produce, and its green depends on the fake graph disagreeing with Cypher MERGE. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT - it is the test's own input. The fixture builds two HAS_UNIT edges from archived_temperature to the SAME counterpart unit:eV, differing only in properties.source (archive-primary, archive-secondary). The writer at signed_manifest.py:7407 is MERGE (start)-[relationship:HAS_UNIT]->(end) SET relationship = $properties, whose MERGE pattern carries no property predicate, so in Neo4j the second write MATCHES the first and overwrites its properties: one relationship, live count 1. The test double at test_archive_reconstruction.py:63-72 keys its edge list on the whole tuple INCLUDING properties, so it appends a second edge and reports live 2 - which is the only reason the asserted row (expected 1, archive_census, observed 2) exists. DEMONSTRATED, not argued: re-running that exact authority against the same fixture with only the edge store re-keyed on (start, type, end) - MERGE-faithful, nothing else changed - the apply REFUSES with SignedManifestConflict 'archive-versus-live relationship counts differ' and one edge is stored, because the closure expects HAS_UNIT 2 while live holds 1 (signed_manifest.py:7425-7432). Log: /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260921T085204284424-review-of-the-receipt-shows-which-source-set-each-expectation/merge-fidelity-probe.log, probe: /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260921T085204284424-review-of-the-receipt-shows-which-source-set-each-expectation/merge_fidelity_probe.py. Two consequences. The receipt row this test locks is unreachable through the committed path for this authority, so the test cannot fail for the production reason it claims to guard; and anyone who later makes the double model MERGE correctly gets a SignedManifestConflict error out of a test whose name is about precedence. THE REPAIR IS CHEAP AND KEEPS THE PROPERTY: the disagreement is genuinely reachable with two DISTINCT counterparts - give the second edge counterpart_id unit:keV (declared in the authority's counterparts, label Unit per _ARCHIVE_EDGE_COUNTERPARTS) and keep archive_roles HAS_UNIT 1. Closure 2, live 2, census 1 all hold, the loader's reconstructable >= count guard at signed_manifest.py:6942 passes since 2 >= 1, the apply's parity check passes since live 2 equals closure 2, and the same row (expected 1, archive_census, observed 2) is asserted - this time from a state the writer really can reach.

MUST-FIX (misreport, one-line edit): the landed evidence document records the code commit as 'Landed 2026-09-21 at 3c47fa002d79947424110199ee119ccfc4ee50a1', and no object with that hash exists. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT: git cat-file -e 3c47fa002d79947424110199ee119ccfc4ee50a1 in any clone exits non-zero, and git show on it reports an unknown revision; git rev-parse 3c47fa002 returns the real 3c47fa00277b8c9347efc7031679dc6e23b11ebc. The first nine characters match, so the value reads as a full SHA and fails only when someone tries to use it - which is the whole purpose of recording a revision in an evidence document. The same invented value appears in the worker manifest's commits list and in after_suite.revision, so a coordinator auditing the node by its declared revision cannot resolve it either. The base SHA a0d303ca47357821f4a1f595d8a8089e462b32fa in the same sentence is correct and resolves, which is why the line does not look wrong. Repair: substitute the output of git rev-parse at the three sites; never retype a hash.

NOT MUST-FIX, recorded so it is not re-derived: the receipt reader is defensive about the container and strict about the row. Line 8466 takes receipt.get('identity_role_parity') or {}, then 8469 and 8474 index role_counts['expected'] and role_counts['expected_source'] directly. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT: any receipt whose parity rows omit expected_source - which today cannot be constructed, because the sole producer sets the key in all three branches, so this is a latent shape rather than a live defect. It is worth knowing because the failure mode is a KeyError traceback out of an operator command AFTER the transaction has committed, at the moment the operator is reading what the apply did; the receipt lines already printed would be the only record. If a second producer is ever added, the invariant to carry with it is the one this node established: a parity row names its source or it is not a parity row.

FOLLOW-ON, outside this node's fence and reported rather than triaged: a preview prints no parity information at all, and that silence is indistinguishable from an applied receipt with an empty parity set. The preview and refused receipts composed at signed_manifest.py:7346-7357 carry identity_roles but no identity_role_parity key, so 'receipt.get(...) or {}' yields {} and the loop emits nothing. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT: imas-codex sn restore apply <authority> --reason '...' without --apply prints the outcome line, any refusals, and manifest_sha256, and zero parity lines - so the expectation provenance this node added is visible only on the run that has already committed. An operator deciding whether to authorise the apply sees none of it. This is pre-existing and unchanged by this node; it is the natural next node if the receipt's purpose is to inform the decision rather than to document it afterwards.

POSITIVE, recorded so it is not re-derived: the Click test is a real guard, not a restatement. test_cli_receipt_names_an_unestablished_expectation_source drives the committed command through CliRunner with apply_signed_manifest monkeypatched, asserts the exact line 'parity archived_temperature EVIDENCED_BY: expected unestablished source neither observed 0' AND asserts 'expected None' not in output, so either half of the declared mutation - dropping the source token, or restoring the bare Python rendering - turns it red on its own. negative-control-cli-output.log confirms it: mutation line first, '1 failed' last, one test collected. This also closes a surface that had no test before: no other test in the repository asserted any part of the restore-apply parity rendering. Before editing either assertion, note that they are not redundant - the membership assertion is what forbids a future formatter from printing the source token while still rendering None for the count.

justifications.durability: The CLI half is durably pinned; the precedence half is pinned to a fake's behaviour rather than to the system's. CAN THE CHANGE BE INVERTED WITH THE SUITE STILL GREEN - no for either half, and the controls demonstrate it: dropping the source token or restoring the bare Python None each fails test_cli_receipt_names_an_unestablished_expectation_source, because that test asserts the whole line and additionally asserts 'expected None' not in output, so either half of the mutation alone is caught. DOES THE NEW INVARIANT HOLD AT EVERY CONSTRUCTION SITE INCLUDING FALLBACK AND EXCEPT PATHS - yes: 'every parity row names its source' has exactly one construction site, and all three of its branches set expected_source in the same dict literal, so there is no fallback path that can emit a row without it; the applied branch's except path (7451-7454) rolls back and re-raises without composing a receipt, and the preview branch composes no parity at all. DOES ANY EXISTING TEST ASSERT THE BEHAVIOUR THE CHANGE REPLACED - no, and I checked rather than assumed: no test in tests/ asserted the old CLI line at all (the restore-apply CLI tests at test_archive_reconstruction_entry_point.py:318-371 assert the adapter is reached and the digest rules, never the parity rendering), so the change replaced an uncovered surface and deleted no assertion. The durability deduction is FINDING 1: the precedence test's green depends on the fake graph writing two relationships where the real MERGE writes one, so correcting the fake later turns this test into an error rather than a precedence signal.
justifications.evidence: Strong measurements, one misreported identifier that has landed in the repository. Every cited log was opened. negative-control-precedence.log and negative-control-cli-output.log each begin with their declared mutation verbatim and each end '1 failed', and each drives exactly the one test it claims. baseline-standard-names.log and after-standard-names.log both completed (exit 1 on a red base) with identical 20 failures and 3 setup errors, 7515 then 7517 passed: zero added failures, exactly two added passes, which matches the two new tests. The pre-repair reversal run recording 22 failures is the honest correction of the prior review's stale claim and it is kept in the evidence document. I re-ran the four related files at HEAD in my own worktree: 42 passed in 12.62s (review-focused.log). THE MISREPORT: the code commit's full SHA is given as 3c47fa002d79947424110199ee119ccfc4ee50a1 in the manifest's commits list, in after_suite.revision, and - the one that matters - at line 774 of the landed evidence document. git cat-file -e on that value fails; git rev-parse 3c47fa002 returns 3c47fa00277b8c9347efc7031679dc6e23b11ebc. The short prefix is real and the remaining 31 hex digits are invented, so an auditor pasting the recorded revision gets 'unknown revision' rather than the diff. See FINDING 2.
justifications.fit: The change reads like the code around it. The CLI edit is five lines at the one site that renders parity, lifts expected into a local before formatting rather than nesting a conditional inside the f-string, and keeps the existing one-line-per-role shape. The test file reuses the established fixture helpers from test_archive_reconstruction rather than rebuilding a graph double, and the new edges parameter threaded through the local _apply_authority helper is defaulted so the three pre-existing callers are untouched. Docstrings state the mechanism and carry no plan, ticket or stage label; commit subjects are conventional with bodies; grep -Eic for co-authored-by, generated with, claude, copilot over both commit messages returns 0. One asymmetry worth naming: the reader takes the container defensively (receipt.get('identity_role_parity') or {}) and then indexes the row strictly (role_counts['expected_source']) - FINDING 3, not reachable today.
justifications.goal_fidelity: VERDICT MUST-FIX, on the test fixture and on a landed revision string; the production behaviour itself is SOUND. Read from the landed diff at the integrated head, not from the worker's report: both node commits are ancestors of HEAD 5fbf21830 (git merge-base --is-ancestor returns 0 for 3c47fa00277b8c9347efc7031679dc6e23b11ebc and e061c2fe9bd9a7840be7f88e907d1b9f54ff82bc), and the marker the change INTRODUCED is present there - git show HEAD:imas_codex/cli/sn.py holds expected_display at 8470 and role_counts['expected_source'] at 8474, and both new test names are in HEAD:tests/standard_names/test_archive_parity_receipt.py. THE THREE FENCED QUESTIONS. (1) DOES THE NEW TEST FAIL FOR THE RIGHT REASON - YES for the precedence, and I confirmed the control rather than trusting it. The recorded control rebinds signed_manifest._archive_role_parity to a closure-first variant; the call site at signed_manifest.py:7446 resolves that name through the module global, so the rebinding does take effect, and negative-control-precedence.log opens with the mutation line verbatim and ends '1 failed'. The assertion that moves is the precedence pair (expected 1 / archive_census becomes expected 2 / reconstruction_closure), not an incidental fixture difference. BUT the state it pins cannot occur in production - see FINDING 1. (2) IS AN UNESTABLISHED EXPECTATION DISTINGUISHABLE FROM A RECORDED NULL IN EVERY CASE - YES, and the loader is what makes it total. _load_archive_role_counts (signed_manifest.py:6934-6941) refuses any census count that is not a non-negative int and rejects bool, so an archive census can never carry a null; and the three branches of _archive_role_parity (7272-7281) make expected None if and only if expected_source is 'neither'. A recorded count of zero renders 'expected 0 source archive_census', an unestablished one renders 'expected unestablished source neither'; the words cannot collide because expected is int|None and 'unestablished' is not an int. The source token printed beside it is what makes the two readable even if a future producer did emit a null under a named source. (3) DOES ANY OTHER CONSUMER OF THE PARITY MAPPING STILL PRINT ONLY EXPECTED AND OBSERVED - NO, there is no other consumer. grep -rn identity_role_parity over imas_codex/ returns exactly one producer (signed_manifest.py:7446) and exactly one reader (cli/sn.py:8466); every other hit is a test. The preview and refused receipts (signed_manifest.py:7346-7357) carry no identity_role_parity key at all, which the reader's 'or {}' absorbs - see FINDING 4, which is pre-existing and out of this node's scope.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exact. git diff --stat 3c47fa002^..e061c2fe9 is four files and precisely the four declared write paths: imas_codex/cli/sn.py, tests/standard_names/test_archive_parity_receipt.py, docs/evidence/archive/paid-identity-deletion-protection-landed.html and docs/plans/paid-identity-deletion-protection.html, 119 insertions and 2 deletions with no stray file. The split is clean - code and test in 3c47fa002, documents in e061c2fe9 - the generated models and .env are untouched, nothing outside the fence was edited, and the worktree was left clean. No branch was created, no merge or push was performed.
